# When both branches change the same region of a secret, the secret merge driver
# writes git conflict markers into the REVEALED (gitignored) plaintext. git never
# sees them - the tracked object is ciphertext - so the pre-commit finalize scans
# for them and refuses to seal until they are resolved. Otherwise the markers
# would be silently encrypted into the object.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

cp base.txt $TMPDIR/base.txt
cp ours.txt $TMPDIR/ours.txt
cp theirs.txt $TMPDIR/theirs.txt

exec sesam init --user admin --install-merge
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt db.txt
exec sesam add db.txt --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add db'

# OURS and THEIRS change the SAME line, so the merge cannot combine them.
exec git checkout -b ours
cp $TMPDIR/ours.txt db.txt
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours'

exec git checkout -b theirs ours~1
cp $TMPDIR/theirs.txt db.txt
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'theirs'

# Merge: content conflict -> markers land in the revealed db.txt, and the driver
# reports the conflict count on stderr.
exec git checkout ours
! exec git merge theirs
stderr 'automatically merging revealed file db.txt; 1 conflict - please fix manually'
grep '^<<<<<<< ' db.txt
grep '^>>>>>>> ' db.txt

# Finalizing without resolving the markers is refused - the seal would bake them
# into the ciphertext, and git itself can't catch it.
exec git add -A
! exec git commit --no-edit
stderr 'unresolved merge conflict markers'

# Resolve the markers in the revealed file; the finalize then succeeds and the
# committed merge verifies (no markers sealed into the object).
cp $TMPDIR/ours.txt db.txt
exec git commit --no-edit
exec sesam verify
! grep '^<<<<<<< ' db.txt

-- base.txt --
line1
SECRET = BASE
line3
-- ours.txt --
line1
SECRET = OURS
line3
-- theirs.txt --
line1
SECRET = THEIRS
line3
